thread:
carmen: Hey team — escalated ticket from FinTech customer. They report SSE streams frequently drop after ~60s with partial output (client gets a couple "data:" chunks then connection closes). Customer says this started after they moved through our EU gateway. Ticket: T-45219. Request-id in logs: rq_0a1b2c3d.

liam: Can you paste the client's raw output and our proxy logs for that request-id? Also which SDK / browser are they using?

carmen: Client is a Node backend using eventsource-polyfill (server-to-server polling style). Client log excerpt: 

```
data: {"id":"msg_1","text":"partial text..."}

# ~30s silence

Error: Connection reset
    at TLSSocket.onread (internal/stream_base_commons.js:...)
```

And our edge logs for rq_0a1b2c3d (redacted):

```
EDGE: accept connection from 10.2.12.5 -> open stream
APP: stream started, model=redwood-xl, session=xyz
EDGE: no data forwarded for 65s
PROXY: upstream read timed out -> closing connection (code: 504 read_timeout)
```

carmen: Customer saw HTTP 200 initially, then a FIN from gateway after ~65s, no 5xx in their client, just sudden socket close.

alex: That log line "no data forwarded for 65s" screams idle timeout at the load-balancer/proxy. Are we sending comment pings (colon lines) on the stream? If not, intermediaries may tear down the TCP connection.

maya: Do we have ALB/ELB timeouts set to 60s in that region? Default ALB idle timeout is 60s unless changed. Also some ISP proxies will drop idle connections aggressively.

carmen: We don't have colon pings in this customer's deployment — they rely on the client sending application keepalives. Customer says they don't send regular heartbeats.

liam: Repro steps from our side? Can we run curl -v -N against the same stream to see whether the gateway closes without any data from server?

carmen: Yep repro command provided to customer and ran in staging: 

```
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?session=xyz" > out.log
# wait ~70s -> connection closed by server
```

carmen: out.log shows the first two data events then connection reset by peer.

alex: Quick mitigation: we should enable server-side comment pings (send ":\n\n" every 15s) for streams that are long-running and have no token output. That keeps ALBs and intermediate proxies happy. Also consider enabling TCP keepalive at the kernel/socket level, but many proxies don't forward that.

oncall-sre: I can check ALB idle timeout in EU region. If it's 60s that lines up. We should also check our proxy (nginx/h2 proxy) read_timeout and proxy_buffer settings.

support-bot: Reproduction checklist added to ticket T-45219: 1) run curl -N; 2) tcpdump on client side to observe FIN from edge; 3) check edge/app logs for upstream read timed out; 4) try enabling comment pings on server; 5) temporary customer workaround: set shorter logical chunking in app to emit something every 10s.

maya: Two things to decide: 1) short-term workaround (comment pings in fronting runtime or ask customer to emit heartbeats), 2) longer-term behavior — we should instrument and auto-send pings from runtime when model output stalls for >10s.

carmen: I patched a staging route to inject comment pings every 15s (quick toggle). Customer confirmed on a call that stream stayed open for several minutes and they got subsequent responses. So workaround works.

alex: Proposed eng plan: (a) add optional server-side comment heartbeat feature in runtime (configurable interval, default 15s), (b) expose header for customers to opt-in (e.g., X-Redwood-Heartbeat: comment=15), (c) add metric for "stream disconnected due to idle timeout" by parsing proxy close codes, (d) docs/FAQ on recommended client heartbeats and Last-Event-ID resume semantics.

devx: I'll draft the docs and a quick code example for JS/Node and plain curl. Example to resume with Last-Event-ID and how to react to partial outputs.

oncall-sre: Action items for SRE: verify ALB timeouts across regions, add a dashboard for unexpected stream resets, and update runbook to include "enable comment pings" as first mitigation. I'll assign follow-up to oncall rotation.

eng-bot: Assigned to eng-runtime team. Priority P1 for a small feature to enable comment pings and logging for these disconnects. Ticket: ENG-8764.

liam: One nuance — some clients treat comment pings as noise and close the connection if they don't like unexpected input. We should make the feature opt-in and document it. Also include jitter to avoid synchronized bursts.

carmen: Noted. Customer is happy with the interim workaround and asked for an ETA on a permanent fix. I'll relay the P1 assignment.

alex: Also recommend trying TCP keepalive on dedicated/private deployments with a shorter idle to help NAT devices. But for hosted/public, comment pings are the only reliable approach across middleboxes.

support-bot: Added postmortem checklist and tagging: cause=idle-proxy-timeout, workaround=server-comment-pings, followup=ENG-8764, update-docs=devx.

devx: I'll put together a short "Streaming best practices" doc (heartbeats, Last-Event-ID, reconnect backoff) and link it from our SDK README.

carmen: Thanks all. I'll close the customer loop and mark ticket as "escalated->eng". :thumbsup:

maya: I'll follow up with infra to see if we can raise ALB idle in specific customer routes while we roll the runtime change.

oncall-sre: Updated runbook entry and created a monitoring alert for spike in 504 read_timeout closes.

alex: Follow-ups: ENG-8764 spec by Fri, canary rollout next Wed, docs update same week.

carmen: Closing notes for ticket: root cause likely intermediate proxy idle timeout causing TCP close when server doesn't emit anything; temporary fix = comment pings; long-term = runtime opt-in heartbeat + metrics + docs.

liam: Great thread. Thanks for the quick repro and staging test.

carmen: :white_check_mark:
